Topic: The Mystery of Pi in Block Collisions

Target audience: Undergraduate students in Physics or Computer Science

Section: section_1 — The Setup: Elastic Collisions

Lecture lines:
Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
Momentum and energy are conserved in elastic collisions.
Consider a massive block hitting a small one.

Planned animations:
Create two colored squares on screen (#FF0000, #00FF00).
Animate squares colliding elastically in center screen.
Show velocity vectors updating after collision.
Label velocity vectors as v1 and v2.
Flash the collision point to emphasize interaction.

Section: section_2 — Visualizing the Collision Count

Lecture lines:
Add a wall behind the smaller block.
The block bounces between the wall and big block.
A counter tracks the total number of collisions.

Planned animations:
Display a counter starting at zero.
Increment counter each time spheres collide.
Highlight the counter text when it updates.

Section: section_3 — The Mathematical Bridge

Lecture lines:
Increasing mass ratios change the collision count.
Mass ratio 100 yields 31 collisions.
Mass ratio 10,000 yields 314 collisions.
The count converges to digits of Pi.
This links simple physics to transcendental numbers.

Planned animations:
Show MathTex formula for collision.
Morph formula to show conservation laws.
Highlight conserved terms with #FFFF00.

Section: section_4 — Geometric Interpretation

Lecture lines:
Phase space visualizes collision states as trajectories.
Reflections happen within a V-shaped mirror wedge.
The trajectory angle depends on the mass ratio.
Reflections count the slope to escape the wedge.
Geometry interprets the physical collision count.

Planned animations:
Display a unit circle on canvas.
Animate point reflecting across a line.
Show the angle change of reflection.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Intuition

Lecture lines:
Discrete collisions map to digits of Pi.
Laws of physics constrain the system.
Simple interactions compute complex mathematical truths.

Planned animations:
Sum up total collisions seen.
Fade in final summary text.
Highlight key intuition result.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
